title.narrative: Interpeace - Psychosocial strengthening in Burkina Faso 2023-2025
Interpeace - Psykosocial förstärkning i Burkina Faso 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Den föreslagna insatsen syftar till att verkar för att strategier, planer och insatser av nationella och internationella aktörer, som arbetar i samhällen som drabbats av bristande säkerhet och humanitära kriser, integrerar psykisk hälsa, psykosocialt stöd och utveckling av försörjningsmöjligheter som ett holistiskt tillvägagångssätt för fredsbyggande.
I detta syfte kommer insatsen arbeta för att uppnå tre resultat:
1. Förbrättrad förståelse för konfliktens och osäkerhetens inverkan på den psykiska hälsan, det psykosociala välmåendet, den sociala sammanhållningen, försörjningsmöjligheterna och de viktigaste behoven hos dem som drabbas (före detta medlemmar av säkerhets- och försvarsstyrkorna, regeringsanknutna miliser, lokala säkerhetsinitiativ (Dozos), väpnade grupper samt deras familjer, internflyktingar och deras värdsamhällen) av säkerhetskrisen och den humanitära krisen i Cascades regionen, med beaktande av jämställdhetsperspektivet.
2. Stärkandet och tillgängliggörandet av verktyg och kapacitet för att tillgodose de multidimensionella behoven av psykisk hälsa, psykosocialt stöd och försörjningsmöjligheter hos de befolkningar som drabbats av säkerhetskriser och humanitära kriser, i samband med social sammanhållning och fredsbyggande.
3. Framtagandet av ett nationellt ramverk för multidimensionella vårdåtaganden som integrerar psykisk hälsa, psykosocialt stöd, försörjningsmöjligheter och social sammanhållning.

Interpeace proposes to work towards the following global objective: strategies, plans and interventions of national and international actors working in communities affected by security and humanitarian crises integrate mental health, psychosocial support and livelihoods development as a holistic peacebuilding approach.
Interpeace proposed to attain the global objective by working towards three results:
1. Improved knowledge of the impact of conflict and insecurity on mental health, psychosocial support, social cohesion, livelihoods and the primary needs of affected people (former members of the Security and Defense forces (SFD), government-affiliated militias, local security initiatives (Dozos), armed groups, as well their families, internally displaced people and their host communities) by the security and humanitarian crises in the Cascades region is generated, taking into account the gender dimension
2. Tools and capacities to respond to the multidimensional needs related to mental health, psychosocial support and livelihoods of populations affected by the security and humanitarian crises, in relation to social cohesion and and peacebuilding are strengthened and made available;
3. A national multidimensional care commitment framework that integrates mental health, psychosocial support, livelihoods and social cohesion is developed.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Result 1
Interpeace has undertaken participatory research with the aim to improve knowledge on how conflict and insecurity affects mental health in Burkina Faso. The research resulted in the report Strengthening psychosocial wellbeing for sustainable peace: participatory analysis of the impact of the security crisis on mental health, social cohesion and livelihoods of populations in the Cascades region. The research results identify clinical profiles of people affected by the security crisis in the Cascades region and advocate for an approach that integrates mental health, livelihoods and social cohesion. The report suggests actions to inspire public policies and programmatic initiatives. The report has been disseminated to national authorities, UN agencies, international development cooperation and NGOs and associations through a validation workshop.
Result 2
An assessment was conducted using a representative sample of 160 internally displaced people (IDPs) and 20 members of the host community, including local security initiatives. The assessment covered the prevalence of mental disorders, somatic diseases, social problems (food, housing, employment, etc.) and factors causing mental illness. Risk factors identified included: loss of material goods the loss of loved ones lack of prospects and uncertainty about the future precarious living conditions and various traumas (witnessing scenes of violence, kidnapping of close relatives). The assessment revealed that IDPs do not have access to mental health services due to lack of information and awareness.
Based on the assessment, three types of protocols were developed and tested: an initial assessment or screening protocol a group therapy protocol focused on resilience and an individual care protocol.
Training modules to support mental health and psychosocial support practitioners, including health workers, psychologists, educators, local mediators were developed. The training modules were administered to the technical staff of the Association of Volunteers for the Promotion of Social Dimensions of Health (AVPDSS), responsible for implementing the protocols. Four people were trained, namely two social workers, a psychiatrist and a psychologist.
Individual therapy, group therapy and participation in economic recovery activities were offered to 60 participants.
Individual therapy: Individual therapy was a prerequisite to group therapy, the number of sessions varied according to the severity of each case.
Group therapy: The group therapy had five stages: making contact (1) understanding the psychological and socio-community state of the participants (2) strengthening socioemotional resilience (3) strengthening relational and socioeconomic capacities (4) and community engagement (5).
Economic recovery of people affected by the security crisis: Sixty individual microprojects were set up and the participants were trained in entrepreneurship, with the assistance of the regional management in charge of Humanitarian Action in the Cascades region.
Result 3
Communication and sharing of research results and protocols has helped to generate commitment from decentralized actors for care that integrates mental health, psychosocial support, livelihoods and social cohesion. At the end of the project, institutional communication and interinstitutional collaboration initiated within the technical committee allowed various actors to become aware of the need to move towards a more holistic approach.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
